contexts.finding: Arterial connexin deletion reduces selected coupling readouts and restricts or delays propagated cortical vascular responses. Local and far-bin nulls, remaining small-vessel tracing and alternative carriers constrain a complete mechanism.
limitations: Adult mice of both sexes, overall age range 8-41 weeks. BMX:CreERT2 Gja4fl/fl Gja5fl/fl animals and Cre-negative double-floxed controls both receive tamoxifen. The driver targets arterial endothelium beyond the brain, including aorta; it is not a capillary-only or brain-only intervention. Assay-specific age/sex distributions are not fully resolved.

No prospective sample-size calculation. Genotype-blinded functional imaging acquisition and randomized stimulus order are reported; random stimulus order is not random genotype allocation. Pre-unblinding exclusions lack a complete animal manifest. The Gja4 floxed allele has an oocyte hypomorphism; same-flox controls do not establish equivalence to wild-type physiology.

Aortic electrophysiology uses six cells from only two mice per genotype; tracer loading uses six control and eight mutant fills from two mice per genotype. Cell-level tests do not supply six or eight independent animals. Apparent capacitance includes the coupled network, not just one cell surface. These are aortic recordings, not brain endothelial voltage recordings.

Retinal SERT tracing uses viral overexpression and terminal transcardial serotonin loading under anesthesia, 6-9 weeks after tamoxifen. Large-artery spreading events require favorable loading and occurred in only two of four controls; single-cell fills occurred in all four mutants. This selected qualitative tracing cannot determine a population conductance or physiological serotonin pathway.

Cx37, Cx40, Cx43 and Cx45 reporter distributions describe vascular segments; expression alone does not measure coupling strength or signal direction. Small-vessel tracer persistence is qualitative. A two-gene arterial deletion does not isolate the function of each isoform or test a selective isoform swap.

Focal visual two-photon imaging measures relative diameter; widefield IOS measures an optical HbT-related response. Neither IOS nor the derived response-propagation speed is a calibrated blood-flow, RBC-velocity, oxygen-use or electrical-conduction measurement. General functional analyses select arteries with baseline diameter greater than 15 micrometers.

Visual activity distance uses normalized, thresholded widefield GCaMP, which is biased toward upper cortical layers. The threshold does not prove absence of deeper or sparse activity. Optogenetic distance instead uses a postmortem ChRmine-expression mask, not simultaneous firing measurements. Histological arterial masks are manually registered and refined, not generated causal geometry.

Motion, pupil and locomotion corrections and signal-selection rules affect the analyzed response. In two-photon processing, selected low-power traces are set to zero by an analysis rule. Linear mixed models account for nesting in functional comparisons; the separate resting-diameter test treats vessels as independent despite nesting within mice.

Optogenetic stimulation uses two-second ChRmine pulse trains and six mice per genotype. The zero-laser condition can retain spontaneous vasomotion and imaging-light opsin activation; it is not an opsin-negative control. Functional imaging days 14-16 after viral injection do not specify a universal post-tamoxifen interval.

Propagation velocity is derived from the inverse slope of optical-response onset time versus position along a selected artery, with onset at ten percent of a sigmoid fit. Figure 5E calls it the slope, whereas Methods specify the inverse. Velocity analysis reports thirty averaged repeats, while the general optogenetic protocol reports ninety per power across sessions; subset selection requires clarification.

Full-screen noise differs from focal circles in spatial coverage and pattern. The comparison does not isolate energetic demand, and oxygen consumption or ATP supply is not measured. Time-to-peak genotype differences depend on distance bin; the farthest optogenetic and full-field bins are nonsignificant, not evidence of equivalence.

Resting microvascular control measures capillary RBC velocity near 100 micrometers depth, not whole-brain perfusion or RBC flux. Tail-cuff systolic/diastolic pressure is a separate systemic control. Nonsignificance in these small cohorts does not demonstrate physiological equivalence.

Exact-title/DOI searches identified no correction resolving the listed discrepancies; this is not exhaustive notice surveillance. Final-versus-in-press supplementary pagination remains unresolved.
contexts.finding: Arterial connexin deletion reduces selected coupling readouts and restricts or delays propagated cortical vascular responses. Local and far-bin nulls, remaining small-vessel tracing and alternative carriers constrain a complete mechanism.
limitations: Adult mice of both sexes, overall age range 8-41 weeks. BMX:CreERT2 Gja4fl/fl Gja5fl/fl animals and Cre-negative double-floxed controls both receive tamoxifen. The driver targets arterial endothelium beyond the brain, including aorta; it is not a capillary-only or brain-only intervention. Assay-specific age/sex distributions are not fully resolved.

No prospective sample-size calculation. Genotype-blinded functional imaging acquisition and randomized stimulus order are reported; random stimulus order is not random genotype allocation. Pre-unblinding exclusions lack a complete animal manifest. The Gja4 floxed allele has an oocyte hypomorphism; same-flox controls do not establish equivalence to wild-type physiology.

Aortic electrophysiology uses six cells from only two mice per genotype; tracer loading uses six control and eight mutant fills from two mice per genotype. Cell-level tests do not supply six or eight independent animals. Apparent capacitance includes the coupled network, not just one cell surface. These are aortic recordings, not brain endothelial voltage recordings.

Retinal SERT tracing uses viral overexpression and terminal transcardial serotonin loading under anesthesia, 6-9 weeks after tamoxifen. Large-artery spreading events require favorable loading and occurred in only two of four controls; single-cell fills occurred in all four mutants. This selected qualitative tracing cannot determine a population conductance or physiological serotonin pathway.

Cx37, Cx40, Cx43 and Cx45 reporter distributions describe vascular segments; expression alone does not measure coupling strength or signal direction. Small-vessel tracer persistence is qualitative. A two-gene arterial deletion does not isolate the function of each isoform or test a selective isoform swap.

Focal visual two-photon imaging measures relative diameter; widefield IOS measures an optical HbT-related response. Neither IOS nor the derived response-propagation speed is a calibrated blood-flow, RBC-velocity, oxygen-use or electrical-conduction measurement. General functional analyses select arteries with baseline diameter greater than 15 micrometers.

Visual activity distance uses normalized, thresholded widefield GCaMP, which is biased toward upper cortical layers. The threshold does not prove absence of deeper or sparse activity. Optogenetic distance instead uses a postmortem ChRmine-expression mask, not simultaneous firing measurements. Histological arterial masks are manually registered and refined, not generated causal geometry.

Motion, pupil and locomotion corrections and signal-selection rules affect the analyzed response. In two-photon processing, selected low-power traces are set to zero by an analysis rule. Linear mixed models account for nesting in functional comparisons; the separate resting-diameter test treats vessels as independent despite nesting within mice.

Optogenetic stimulation uses two-second ChRmine pulse trains and six mice per genotype. The zero-laser condition can retain spontaneous vasomotion and imaging-light opsin activation; it is not an opsin-negative control. Functional imaging days 14-16 after viral injection do not specify a universal post-tamoxifen interval.

Propagation velocity is derived from the inverse slope of optical-response onset time versus position along a selected artery, with onset at ten percent of a sigmoid fit. Figure 5E calls it the slope, whereas Methods specify the inverse. Velocity analysis reports thirty averaged repeats, while the general optogenetic protocol reports ninety per power across sessions; subset selection requires clarification.

Full-screen noise differs from focal circles in spatial coverage and pattern. The comparison does not isolate energetic demand, and oxygen consumption or ATP supply is not measured. Time-to-peak genotype differences depend on distance bin; the farthest optogenetic and full-field bins are nonsignificant, not evidence of equivalence.

Resting microvascular control measures capillary RBC velocity near 100 micrometers depth, not whole-brain perfusion or RBC flux. Tail-cuff systolic/diastolic pressure is a separate systemic control. Nonsignificance in these small cohorts does not demonstrate physiological equivalence.
